title: Learning Loops
hook: Making the same mistake twice usually means the lesson never got written down.
statement: Treat failures as data you feed straight back into your next attempt.
explainer: People who improve fast aren't more talented. They turn a failure into a specific change before the sting fades. That's what stops the same mistake coming back.
sop: Write down what happened within 24 hours. Facts, not feelings.
Pull out one specific change to make, not 'try harder.'
Pick your Rate: a small tweak or a bigger shift.
Use the change on your very next attempt.
Track whether the New Tactic actually did better.
equation_example: Old tactic scores 6, Error is -3, Rate is 0.5. 6 + (-3 × 0.5) = 4.5, your adjusted approach. A higher Rate means you adjust fast after one miss. Too high overreacts to noise. Too low repeats the mistake.
question: Pick one recent failure and write the specific change you'll make next time.
closing_statement: A failure without a written lesson repeats itself.
caption:
Principle Nº 211: Learning Loops

Making the same mistake twice usually means the lesson never got written down.

Treat failures as data you feed straight back into your next attempt.

Your turn: Pick one recent failure and write the specific change you'll make next time.
